t: The most extensive of the first urban civilisations, it covered more ground than Egypt and Mesopotamia together, with over a thousand known sites and great cities such as Harappa and Mohenjo-daro.
Its builders laid out streets on a grid, used bricks of standard proportions and drained whole neighbourhoods with covered sewers, yet left no palaces, royal tombs or images of war.
Its short inscriptions remain undeciphered, so its language, rulers and beliefs are known only through archaeology and through Mesopotamian texts that call it Meluhha.
dyk: A cylinder seal of the time of the Akkadian Empire, now in the Louvre, belonged to a man named Shu-ilishu, who called himself “interpreter of the Meluhhan language”: Mesopotamians needed translators to deal with traders from the Indus.
ev: Farmers settle at Mehrgarh in Balochistan, beginning the long prelude to the Indus cities
The Early Harappan phase begins, with farming villages and small towns across the Indus plains
The mature phase begins: Harappa, Mohenjo-daro and other cities are laid out with grid streets and drains
Sargon of Akkad boasts of ships from Meluhha, Magan and Dilmun moored at his capital
The cities decline, and seals, script and standard weights fall out of use
The last Late Harappan cultures give way to the new village cultures of northern India
Excavations at Harappa under Daya Ram Sahni and at Mohenjo-daro under R. D. Banerji uncover the same seals
John Marshall announces the discovery of a forgotten civilisation of the Indus

f.homeland: The plains of the Indus and of the seasonal Ghaggar-Hakra river and their borderlands, in most of present-day Pakistan and north-western India, from Balochistan and Sindh to Punjab, Haryana and Gujarat, with an outpost at Shortughai in Afghanistan
f.period: c. 3300–1300 BCE: the Early Harappan phase from c. 3300 BCE, the mature urban phase c. 2600–1900 BCE, then the Late Harappan phase of villages until c. 1300 BCE
f.known: Planned cities of baked brick with wells and covered drains; the Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro; carved stamp seals with an undeciphered script; standard weights; trade by sea with Mesopotamia
f.sources: Excavations since the 1920s at Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Kalibangan, Lothal, Dholavira, Rakhigarhi and many smaller sites; some 4,000 to 5,000 short inscriptions, still unread; Mesopotamian texts on the trade with Meluhha
